config.basis: every industry against row 0, every class against column 0
config.floor: sd of the year-over-year change in the same square, divided by sqrt(2)

criteria.criterion: a separable field has every square zero, and the basis spans the rest
criteria.detail: separable in, every square zero: worst 8.88e-16 over 20 tables. An arbitrary square rebuilt from four basis squares against the direct calculation: worst 4.44e-16 over 400 draws. So the 17 by (J-1) basis spans them and nothing is being counted twice.
criteria.name: B106-16

criteria.criterion: the squares themselves against a floor measured from this panel's own year-to-year noise
criteria.detail: 188,054 independent squares over 621 country-year tables, 17 classes against a reference class and every industry against a reference industry. Floor measured from this panel's own year-to-year change in the same square, 176,715 pairs: 0.1766 in log points. |square| median 0.3925, p90 1.3444, max 6.9888. Above the floor: 139,811 (74.3%); above twice it 101,142 (53.8%). Median square is 2.22 times the floor. Floor by lag, where a longer lag carries more real drift and so is an upper bound on the noise: 1y 0.1766 clears 74.3%, 2y 0.2346 clears 66.9%, 5y 0.3470 clears 54.4%. The competing reading puts every one of these at exactly zero.
criteria.name: B106-15

criteria.criterion: the position-scalar reading puts every square at exactly zero
criteria.detail: 139,811 of 188,054 squares (74.3%) stand above the panel's own measured floor of 0.1766 log points, and 101,142 stand above twice it. The median square is 2.22 times the floor and the largest is 6.9888. A point prediction of exactly zero, so PASS here means the prediction does not hold.

grid_note.ours: two classes at one position are on different terms and the terms are the position's own, so the squares do not vanish

criteria.name: B106-17
criteria.rival_entailment: under that premise p(j,k) = a_j + b_k, so every difference in differences across two positions and two classes cancels term by term and is identically zero. The squares read here are that quantity.
criteria.rival_premise: there is a scalar on the position and a factor for the class, so in logs the pay field is additively separable
